title: Causal carry-bearing coordinates with soft clearance stages
coverage_gap: The two support layouts need only small lateral transfer compared with roughly 0.2 m forward transport. Opposite-sign and extrapolated x factors demand new lateral directions and lengths. A world-action denoiser may memorize the observed y-dominant transfer instead of recomposing direction from ring and peg.
reusable_regularity: After a visible lift with a nearly closed gripper, horizontal carrying can be expressed as forward motion in a frame determined by the ring-to-peg bearing. Use a chunk-start orthonormal yaw mapping, continuously reverting toward native world axes at acquisition and near alignment. Soft acquisition/lift/transport/alignment weights expose clearance and contact structure but never choose an action or execute a state machine. The diffusion model still learns every command.
dependencies_preserved: The bearing comes from goal_xyz minus physical ring_center_xyz, not from the handle site. Handle-hand and handle-ring vectors remain separate.
The yaw only affects x and y. Gravity, hand/ring/peg heights, and the native z command are retained.

Body orientation axes are expressed in the same frame. Cosine and sine plus world hand position preserve native gripper orientation, axis-specific actuation, robot reach and world boundaries; this is not an assertion of exact rotation symmetry of the robot.
All ungated grasp and alignment vectors remain available alongside gated copies, so an erroneous soft stage need not remove the correct relation.
The peg is retained both geometrically and as a height/clearance dependency. There is no planner, collision oracle, success label, hidden reset factor or environment handle.

Absent object2 channels and the redundant native-previous quaternion are not used; native-previous translational kinematics, aperture change, current body axes from both raw observation rows, and measured ring motion are causal.

expected_failure_signature: A slipped ring lifted briefly or an unusual aperture could produce the wrong carry weight; errors should then coincide with frame/stage changes rather than simply absolute x.
Near-target frame regularization trades exact bearing alignment for smoothness; residual lateral oscillation or failure to descend would challenge the 0.04 m stabilizer and soft-alignment hypothesis.

At extreme lateral offsets, the native cube and fixed gripper break yaw symmetry. Saturation, altered transport speed or orientation-dependent grasp errors could remain even with correct ring-relative bearing.
This model has no recovery supervision beyond D_N. Missed grasps can still lead to repeated acquisition or inappropriate motion despite retaining ungated geometry.

required_runtime_fields.source: Only causal_context.raw_history [B,2,42] and raw_current [B,42]; no stored episode phase or time index
required_runtime_fields.representation: 49 physical-scale features per row. Both observation rows are expressed in the same latest chunk-start frame; soft stage features are computed from each available raw row. Earlier-row ring velocity is zero and later-row velocity is their observed difference.
required_runtime_fields.action_frame: Let d=goal-ring at the chunk start, c=lifted_sigmoid*closed_sigmoid, u=c*d_x, v=sqrt(d_y^2+0.04^2). Set sine=u/sqrt(u^2+v^2), cosine=v/sqrt(u^2+v^2). Local xyz=(cosine*world_x-sine*world_y, sine*world_x+cosine*world_y, world_z). Decode by the transpose. The identical orthonormal frame is fixed for all 16 actions, both encode and decode; no future pose or iterative frame updates. Native xyz scale is unchanged. Gripper passes through exactly. Encoded components are not clipped; only the host clips decoded native action4.

support_fit.source: Median obs[0,41] over precisely the two supplied complete D_N episodes
support_fit.purpose: Nonlearned initial ring-height reference for the lift sigmoid; not a time/phase lookup
support_fit.deployment_state: One JSON scalar rest_ring_z_m, explicitly restored before build_modules
support_fit.other_constants: Metric smoothing widths and aperture/clearance feature centers are fixed design choices motivated by observed phases, not tuned performance statistics or success rules.

architecture: Exactly one unmodified common DP with condition_dim=49 and action_dim=4. No auxiliary losses or outside learned controller. Common action epsilon mask normalization and update budget are unchanged.
change_summary: Initial independent scientific design: a causal, soft carry-dependent yaw action representation and clearance-stage feature factorization, rather than identity-action passive relations. No development feedback used.
